answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via cryptographic distance-bounding across wide-baseline verifiers. Agents answer signed nonce challenges from beacons spanning an ocean, which timestamp round-trip delays with a quartz crystal clock. Intersecting these fiber-speed bounds locks one key per physical cell in an umber registry, forcing attackers to lease dispersed hosts per clone. However, adversaries can still spoof bounds using colluding relays or microwave links.
